summary.title: Let's Build a Compiler, by Jack Crenshaw
summary.one_liner: A multi-part tutorial series that walks you through writing a compiler for a small Pascal-like language, building up from expression parsing to procedures and types.
takeaways: The series is organized into 16 parts, from an introduction through parsing, scanning, and language features.
Topics covered include expression parsing, interpreters, control constructs, boolean expressions, and lexical scanning.
Later parts cover a top-down view, a small language called TINY, procedures, types, and unit construction.
Plain text, DOS text, formatted text, and PDF versions of the full series are available as downloads.
summary.summary: This is the index page for Jack Crenshaw's tutorial series "Let's Build a Compiler," hosted on the I.E.C.C. site. It lists 16 numbered parts, from an introduction and expression parsing through interpreters, control constructs, lexical scanning, a top view, a language called TINY, procedures, types, and unit construction. The page links to downloadable ZIP and PDF versions of the full text. The page text itself does not describe the teaching method in detail, so the approach is inferred only from the part titles.
